advances: The largest projective-energy stratum among actual deepest points has exact marked translation equality on all its integer anchored relations, and yields a parity payment for its retained mass.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Sliding a closed containing halfspace to pass through \(Y\) reduces its mass. For each fixed unit ambient normal \(u\), the indicators of the through-\(Y_j\) halfspaces satisfy \(\limsup_j\mathbf1_{H_{Y_j}}\le\mathbf1_{H_Y}\) when \(Y_j\to Y\). Reverse Fatou gives upper semicontinuity of the cap mass, and the infimum over normals is upper semicontinuous. Each depth superlevel is convex because any closed halfspace containing a convex combination contains at least one positively weighted input point. At an interior point of a fiber \(K_p\), every containing halfspace captures at least half of a small ball in that fiber, including the case of an entire fiber trace. Thus compactness of \(S\) gives attainment of \(Q>0\). Outside \(\operatorname{conv}S\) a separating halfspace gives zero depth. It follows that \(D\) is compact and convex.

If \(y\in\partial K_p\), choose a continuous unit normal \(v\) with \(v\cdot y=h_{K_p}(v)\). The anchored hypotheses at \(p\) are exactly those of [155691fc3768c06f](155691fc3768c06f.md). Its supporting slope \(A\) gives
$$
h_{K_z}(v)\le h_{K_p}(v)+A\cdot(z-p)\qquad(z\in P).
$$
The closed halfspace with margin \(v\cdot x-h_{K_p}(v)-A\cdot(z-p)\ge0\) contains \((p,y)\), and each of its fiber traces is empty or contained in a supporting hyperplane, so it has mass zero. Hence \(D\cap S\) consists of own-fiber interior points. The energy root is positive by [d90ba05577427854](d90ba05577427854.md) and continuous on each own interior by finite concavity from [5aeb5916857f97a9](5aeb5916857f97a9.md). Since \(D\cap S\) is compact and there are finitely many fibers, the maximum \(R\) is attained. Strict own-fiber concavity from the same theorem shows that two distinct maximizing marks at one base would yield a larger value at their midpoint in \(D\cap S\). This proves uniqueness.

Take the positive anchored relation in the statement. Its integer target belongs to \(P\) by lattice completeness. Set \(y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_{p_i}\) and \(L=\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i}\). The weighted combination of the interior balls gives \(y\in\operatorname{int}L\), and the anchored inclusion gives \(L\subseteq K_q\). Convexity of \(D\) gives \((q,y)\in D\cap S\). Thus
$$
R\ \ge\ E_{K_q}(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ E_L(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\
\sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_{p_i}}(y_{p_i})^{1/d}=R.
$$
The inclusion and equality conclusions in [5aeb5916857f97a9](5aeb5916857f97a9.md) give \(K_q=L\) and positive homothety of the input marked bodies. Their common energy and \(d\)-homogeneous scaling from [d90ba05577427854](d90ba05577427854.md) make every factor one. The common centered body is consequently also \(K_q-y\). Uniqueness gives \(y=y_q\). Every integer point of \(\operatorname{conv}(J)\) has such a representation, with zero weights omitted, so belongs to \(J\).

Let \(g_p\) be the ordinary centroid of \(K_p\) for \(p\in J\). In a same-parity pair the integer midpoint belongs to \(J\). The relation just proved makes the midpoint body the corresponding average of two translates, with centroid equal to the average of their centroids. Thus the finite weighted graph \(\{(p,g_p):p\in J\}\), with weights \(|K_p|\) and labels the \(k(J)\) occupied parities, meets the midpoint hypothesis of [f4547c4166b39683](f4547c4166b39683.md). It has an atomic centerpoint on the graph of depth at least \(M_J/k(J)\). At that actual point every containing halfspace captures centroids of total graph weight at least \(M_J/k(J)\). For each such centroid the ordinary Grünbaum bound recorded in [c6b7777f667984de](c6b7777f667984de.md), equation (4), pays at least \((d/(d+1))^d\) times its fiber volume. An entire fiber trace pays its full volume. These fiber contributions are disjoint and the other fibers have nonnegative mass. Taking the infimum over halfspaces and then the maximum over \(S\) gives the asserted weak payment.
statement:
Let \(n\ge0\) and \(d\ge1\). Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, and let \(K_p\subset\mathbb R^d\), \(p\in P\), be convex bodies satisfying the anchored inclusions
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i}\subseteq K_q
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_i\ge0,\quad\sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in P.
$$
Put \(S=\bigcup_{p\in P}\{p\}\times K_p\), let \(\mu\) be the sum of fiber volumes on \(S\), and let \(D_\mu(Y)=\inf_{H\ni Y}\mu(H)\) over closed ambient halfspaces. Write \(Q=\max_{Y\in S}D_\mu(Y)\), \(D=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n+d}:D_\mu(Y)\ge Q\}\), and
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{a:\ 1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ \forall x\in K}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx
\quad (y\in\operatorname{int}K).
$$
Then \(Q>0\) is attained, \(D\) is compact and convex, and every \((p,y)\in D\cap S\) has \(y\in\operatorname{int}K_p\). The positive number
$$
R=\max_{(p,y)\in D\cap S}E_{K_p}(y)^{1/d}
$$
is attained. Its attaining bases \(J\) satisfy \(J=\operatorname{conv}(J)\cap\mathbb Z^n\), with a unique attaining mark \(y_p\) at each \(p\in J\). For every \(p_i\in J\) and positive weights \(\lambda_i\) summing to one with \(q=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i\in\mathbb Z^n\),
$$
q\in J,\qquad y_q=\sum_i\lambda_i y_{p_i},\qquad
K_q=\sum_i\lambda_i K_{p_i},\qquad
K_{p_i}-y_{p_i}=K_q-y_q\quad\text{for every }i.
$$
If \(k(J)\) is the number of occupied parities modulo \(2\mathbb Z^n\) and \(M_J=\sum_{p\in J}|K_p|\), then \(Q\ge (d/(d+1))^d M_J/k(J)\).
title: The maximum projective-energy stratum of actual deepest points
